note: HEAR THE PHRASES (13 Nov 2026): the skeleton phrases a pupil must keep, from Michael's Writing Portfolio (data/writing/portfolio.json), word for word, one alternative per slash. 5 introduction, 5 body, 3 conclusion per task; the essay body is 3 per question type, each labelled with the question it answers, so the types can be compared. p = the phrase (… is the pupil's own idea), k = the key word, the one a B2 pupil loses, x = two near-miss traps for k, w = why the key word and not the traps. Maya's recordings: hear-phrases-audio.json (p → mp3).

items.p: Few people would deny that …
items.w: deny that = say it is not true. Refuse is followed by to + verb; reject takes a noun.

items.p: It is widely believed that …
items.w: An adverb before believed: widely. Wide is the adjective; highly goes with recommended, not believed.

items.p: There is considerable debate about whether …
items.w: considerable = large. Considerate means kind to others.

items.p: Some people argue that …, while others believe …
items.w: while joins two contrasting clauses. During takes a noun; meanwhile starts a new sentence.

items.p: It is worth weighing up the advantages and disadvantages of …
items.w: worth + -ing: worth weighing up. Weight is the noun.

items.q: What are the advantages and disadvantages of …?
items.p: The main advantage of … is that …
items.w: The main advantage … is: one advantage, so singular.

items.q: What are the advantages and disadvantages of …?
items.p: A major drawback of … is that …
items.w: A drawback = a disadvantage. A setback is a delay in progress.

items.q: What are the advantages and disadvantages of …?
items.p: While there are many advantages to …, it is also true that …
items.w: it is + adjective: it is also true. Truth is the noun, truly the adverb.

items.p: A major reason why many people agree with … is that it …
items.w: agree with an idea or a person. Agree to a plan; agree on a decision.

items.p: On the other hand, critics argue that … can lead to …
items.w: critics = the people who disagree. Critical is an adjective; criticise is the verb.

items.p: Although both views have merit, I believe that …
items.w: Although + a clause (both views have). Despite takes a noun; However starts a new sentence.

items.p: I firmly believe that … plays an essential role in …
items.w: play a role = have a job or part. A roll is bread; a rule is a law.

items.p: From my perspective, … should be considered a vital part of …
items.w: my perspective = my point of view. Prospective means future (a prospective student).

items.p: There is no doubt in my mind that … is beneficial for …
items.w: is + adjective: beneficial. Benefit is the noun or the verb.

items.p: One possible solution to this problem would be to …
items.w: the solution to a problem: always to.

items.p: The government should take steps to …
items.w: take steps = take action. We never make or do steps.

items.p: If such measures were implemented, … could be significantly reduced.
items.w: Second conditional: if + past (were), then could.

items.q: Why …? What effects does it have?
items.p: One of the main causes of … is …
items.w: One of the + plural noun: one of the main causes.

items.q: Why …? What effects does it have?
items.p: This problem largely results from …
items.w: results from = is caused by. Results in = causes: the opposite direction.

items.q: Why …? What effects does it have?
items.p: As a result, … has become increasingly common.
items.w: An adverb before the adjective common: increasingly.

items.q: How will … change in the future?
items.p: It is likely that … will continue to grow in the coming years.
items.w: It is likely that … is the pattern. Probably is an adverb: it will probably grow.

items.q: How will … change in the future?
items.p: The long-term consequences of this trend may include …
items.w: The consequences … may include: a plural noun. Consequently is a linker.

items.q: How will … change in the future?
items.p: If current patterns persist, … can be expected.
items.w: persist = continue. Insist means demand; resist means fight against.

items.p: On balance, it seems that the benefits of … outweigh the drawbacks.
items.w: outweigh = are greater than. Overweigh and outweight are not words.

items.p: Taking everything into account, …
items.w: take something into account: always into.

items.p: In conclusion, although there are strong arguments on both sides, I firmly believe that …
items.w: although + a clause (there are). Despite takes a noun; even needs though.

items.p: If you are looking for a …, then … could be the perfect option for you.
items.w: look for = try to find. You see or watch something that is already there.

items.p: When it comes to …, few options can compete with …
items.w: compete with = be as good as. Complete means finish; compare is with or to, but means look at differences.

items.p: Are you on the lookout for a …? If so, … could be exactly what you need.
items.w: on the lookout for = searching for. Outlook means a view of the future.

items.p: Known for its …, … has been a favourite among teenagers.
items.w: among a group (teenagers). Between two people or things.

items.p: Having heard so much about …, I was curious to see whether it lived up to its reputation.
items.w: live up to = be as good as people say. Live on means survive; live out means complete.

items.p: What impressed me most was …
items.w: What impressed me: a verb in the past. Impressive is the adjective, impression the noun.

items.p: The real strength of … lies in its …
items.w: lie in = be found in (lies, no object). Lay needs an object: lay the table.

items.p: The thing that is most likely to impress you is …
items.w: be likely to + verb. Probably is an adverb and cannot follow most here.

items.p: Anyone interested in … will be especially impressed by …
items.w: interested in: always in.

items.p: By far the most appealing aspect of … is …
items.w: by far + the most / the best. By much is not English.

items.p: For anyone who is interested in …, … is a must.
items.w: a must = something you have to see or try. A noun here, with a.

items.p: I guarantee that … will not disappoint anyone who is looking for …
items.w: disappoint = not be as good as hoped. Deceive means trick, a false friend of decepcionar.

items.p: I can assure you that … will leave a lasting impression on you.
items.w: a lasting impression = one that stays. Lastly is a linker for the final point.

items.p: The purpose of this report is to examine …
items.w: the purpose = the aim. Propose is a verb; a proposal is a suggestion.

items.p: This report aims to provide a summary of …
items.w: This report aims: he, she, it takes -s.

items.p: This report focuses on …
items.w: focus on: always on.

items.p: The information in this report was collected through a survey among …
items.w: information is uncountable: never informations.

items.p: This report is based on my personal views and experience.
items.w: be based on. Basic is an adjective; basis is a noun (on the basis of).

items.p: It was generally agreed that …
items.w: It was agreed: the passive needs the past participle.

items.p: There was a broad consensus that …
items.w: consensus = what most people agree. A census counts people; consent means permission.

items.p: By far the best aspect of … was that …
items.w: the best aspect … was: one aspect, so singular.

items.p: The highlight of … was …
items.w: The highlight … was: singular noun, singular verb.

items.p: One major criticism expressed by … is …
items.w: a criticism = a complaint. A critic is a person; criticise is the verb.

items.p: In order to …, I would strongly recommend …
items.w: An adverb before recommend: strongly. Hardly means almost not.

items.p: To sum up, the findings clearly show that …
items.w: the findings = what the report found. Founds is not a word.

items.p: The main conclusion to be drawn is that …
items.w: draw, drew, drawn: the passive needs drawn.
